notes: Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on all 8 claims about LysM2's micromolar affinity for chitin. Both LLM and reviewers accept the ITC measurements and mutant validation data as correct.

High overlap (Jaccard=0.571) on LysM2 functional suppression claims. Reviewers accept that LysM2 suppresses immunity experimentally, while LLM rates this UNCERTAIN due to the mechanistic paradox. Both acknowledge the data but differ on confidence level.

Moderate overlap (Jaccard=0.5) on mechanism claims. LLM rates proposed receptor interference mechanism as UNSUPPORTED (explicitly speculative, no direct evidence), while reviewers rate UNCERTAIN (major concern about mechanism but don't definitively reject it).

Shared claim C41 about LysM1 mutant autoactivity. LLM accepts the mutagenesis results as clearly documented, while reviewers express uncertainty due to missing data presentation and lack of statistical analysis.

Shared claim C42 about LysM3 mutants retaining suppression ability. LLM accepts functional validation, while reviewers note pH shifts and request statistical analysis to confirm these mutants are truly not autoactive.
Partial overlap (Jaccard=0.25) on picomolar affinity claims C3 and C53. Both agree the LysM1-LysM3 composite site has sufficient picomolar affinity to function as proposed.
Shared claims C50, C51 about HEK293-produced chitin-free Ecp6. Both accept this protein production method and its functional properties without question.

Shared claims C52, C55 about ITC methodology. LLM accepts the measurements as strongly supporting affinity claims, while reviewers express uncertainty about discrepancies with previous work and request additional controls.

Moderate overlap (Jaccard=0.192) on crystal structure claims C21-C23, C31-C32. Both strongly support the structural analysis, with reviewers explicitly praising it as 'excellent' and a 'significant contribution.'
Shared claims C36-C38 about molecular interactions in the binding groove. Both accept the detailed structural characterization from crystallography without question.

Shared claim C33 about chitin co-purification. LLM accepts this as strong evidence for high-affinity binding, while reviewers question the precise identity and length of the oligomer, requesting mass spectrometry confirmation.
Shared claim C39 about substrate-induced dimerization. LLM accepts this structural feature, while reviewers question whether the binding site is truly substrate-induced or pre-formed.
Shared claim C90 about Ecp6 vs AtCERK1 binding mechanisms. Both accept the structural comparison showing convergent evolution and different binding modes explaining competitive advantage.
Shared claim C68 about dual-mechanism model. Both rate as UNCERTAIN - LLM because second mechanism lacks validation, reviewers because they question how low-affinity LysM2 can function as proposed.

Shared claims C64-C65 about LysM2 mechanism. Both express uncertainty about how LysM2 suppresses immunity given the affinity-concentration mismatch, though reviewers are more explicit about the thermodynamic problem.

LLM result on dual-mechanism conclusion (C68) has only partial peer coverage. Peer R5 addresses mechanism uncertainty but doesn't explicitly evaluate the overall dual-mechanism claim as a distinct conclusion.

LLM result on chitin co-purification (C33-C35, C98-C99) has limited peer coverage. Peer R9 questions C33 specifically but doesn't address the broader biological implications (C34-C35, C98-C99) that LLM evaluates.

LLM result on comparative binding mechanisms (C58-C59, C71, C90) has minimal peer coverage. Only C90 appears in peer results; the detailed structural comparison claims are not explicitly evaluated by reviewers.
